answer: An agent unlocks payout only after three unrelated peers, picked from a juror pool, co-sign its reputation record. Each juror stakes a bond worth a week of its own earnings, and the vouch graph stays public. A farm growing along one vine of puppet wallets still needs three independent jurors to risk real money per puppet, so a thousand fake identities cost three thousand juror bonds that burn when an attestation proves false. Signups are time-boxed: one comet of registrations inside a minute freezes every bond in that wave, and newcomers wait at the jetty while their stake sits locked.
